body_long:
Saint-Barth will have a new festival this winter. Super Island, a first edition, runs for seven days and seven nights, from 27 December 2026 to 2 January 2027, on the beach of Gyp Sea in Saint-Jean Bay.

It brings together two houses born far from the Caribbean. Indie Beach is the Pampelonne beach club of Indie Group, the Saint-Tropez group behind Pablo, Cherry, Playamigos and La Sauvageonne. Gyp Sea belongs to Maisons et Hôtels Sibuet, the family group of Megève, Ménerbes and Saint-Tropez.

## One headliner a night

The line-up gives each night its own name. WhoMadeWho opens on 27 December with a hybrid DJ set. Black Coffee, the Grammy-winning South African DJ, plays on 28 December, and FISHER on 29 December. DJ Tennis and Kaz James play back to back on 30 December.

Peggy Gou takes New Year's Eve. Moojo, Villanova and Matteo Diop follow on 1 January, and the Miami duo Miguelle & Tons close the festival on 2 January.

The beach club becomes the home of the festival for the season, with private cabanas, a lounge, a backstage area and a shared menu that mixes the Mediterranean and the Caribbean. Gyp Sea also sells its beach houses for the week. Ticket prices and capacity are to be confirmed.

## Indie Group settles on the island

The festival is the high point of a full season for Indie Group in Saint-Barth. Pablo Saint-Barth, its rooftop and night bar on the Gustavia harbour, opened last season. A new restaurant, Cream, is announced for December 2026, as a chic and intimate extension of the Pablo universe. Its exact address and opening date are to be confirmed.

On the Gyp Sea side, the Sibuet family turned Villa Marie, on the Colombier hill above Flamands Bay, into Gyp Sea Hotel, with 21 bungalows and villas and one MICHELIN Key, and added beach houses in Saint-Jean.

## The signal

On Saint-Barth, the season is now sold as an event. Two French groups from the Riviera and the Alps are pooling a beach, a brand and a line-up to own the most expensive week of the year.

For hoteliers, the lesson is about programming. A beach club with a festival behind it sells cabanas, villas and dinners well before the first set starts.
